reviews.text:
The staff here is great, no complaints about that. They treated my cat with a lot of care and im grateful i was able to get his eye ulcer examined. HOWEVER, I walked through the doors at not even 2:30pm on a Saturday. My cat didn't start the sedation process until around 11pm and we didn't leave the hospital until 12:30/1am. Every 2 hours i kept getting updates along the lines of "your cat is hanging out in the back with us in his carrier but unfortunately there are more serious cases". Long story short, they kept my cat in a carrier for 8 hours because there were "more serious cases". I can understand one or two cases but to go to an "emergency room" and have to wait to be seen for 8 hours is a bit ridicuous, as it defeats the whole purpose of going to an emergency room.

Aside from the waiting situation, everything else was AMAZING. The doctor was super sweet, very soft spoken and was able to answer every single question i had.

I am so grateful to Blue Pearl in Brooklyn. It is a state of the art animal hospital. The nurses and vets were outstanding and informed me about the care of my cat every step of the way. From the moment I walked in, I was surrounded by kindness, compassion and a feeling of love for all animals.

UPDATE:
About 8 weeks ago, I brought my cat to Blue Pearl and a male vet there, without even examining my cat berated me for not wanting to kill my cat.  (??!!)  My cat is doing just fine since.  I went to a nearby wellness vet and they were puzzled why Blue Pearl said that he should be euthanized/killed.

I previously had been here A LOT, usually overnight, but now it's hard to trust them to be alone with my cat.  God knows what they might do.

Prior to bringing my cat to Blue Pearl, I went to a nearby regular vet and I went back to them after being at Blue Pearl and they said my cat was fine and there was no need to euthanize him. (??) Weirdly, the same thing happened at Verg.*  My cat is still his sweet lovely self and is doing well.  So bizarre.

*At Verg, we got a very hostile intake woman.  She was so hostile that the employee next to her asked her to switch places so that she could assist me, instead.

I used to take my pets to a vet in bay ridge, but they are no longer 24 hours and it was around 8 pm when I knew something wasn’t right with my dog. I got her to BluePearl and explained our situation… they immediately brought her up to emergency, and even though I was a mess and on the verge of a breakdown- the calm demeanor of the staff was comforting. They even offered water, tea, and coffee, which when you are already fighting tears- is sometimes exactly what you need to ground yourself. From the doctor, to the nurse, to the receptionists- everyone was delightful in a not so delightful moment of my life… I hope I (or my pets) never need their services, but if I (or they) do- I will definitely go back to them.
my dog was put down here 3 years ago ❤️
The Service was Wonderful
They are great at what they are doing, they took care of my baby real quick but sadly I lost her .But I thank them for all they did.
Thank you so much for taking the time to leave a review! Your support means everything to us, and we’re grateful for the opportunity to care for your pet.
Thank you for the 5-star rating! We appreciate your trust in our care for your pet!
Your 5-star review means the world to us! We’re so grateful to be a part of your pet’s health journey.

BluePearl is unfortunately where I just spent one of the worst days of my life. My little kitty is so sick but the compassion, care, and empathy everyone at BluePearl exhibits was so comforting despite everything going on. I can’t recommend this animal hospital enough.

While I appreciate the many times that Blue Pearl has helped my cat, I am going to try to stay away from the 3rd street location as there is a vet there who was literally yelling at me to kill my cat.  This was about 6 weeks ago.  I brought my cat to Verg and they didnt understand why Blue Pearl wanted to kill my cat. (A caveat is that a woman at Verg did, indeed, tell me forcefully to kill my cat - as far as I know, she was not a vet but more of a social worker.)  I said no and she, too, screamed at me.  Thankfully, the superstars at the front desk had their vets examine Mocha and they said to take him home and monitor him.  He has been doing well at home since.
Insanely expensive, thousands of dollars a day for our dogs hospital stay. I will never go back here again.
Excellent attention, the very concerned medical team explained every detail to me about my Shih Tzu health  very good attention, from the front desk to the doctors.
My dog received professional, compassionate, effective care, delivered in a timely manner. Communication was clear. Most importantly, my dog is feeling better. Highly recommend.

We had heard many times that BluePearl had a shitty reputation, but honestly thought people were exaggerating. After what happened to Cas, our cat, I completely understand why. The entire experience was a shit show.

Cas is obsessed with food and normally wakes us at 5 a.m. for treats. When he suddenly stopped eating and acting like himself, we knew something was seriously wrong.

At our first visit, Dr. Vazul Munjal told us we “shouldn’t go looking, because we might find something,” and then claimed Cas had heart disease. He did not. What kind of emergency vet discourages someone from looking for answers when their cat is clearly sick?

Things got worse with Dr. Mallika Prabhakar in Internal Medicine. Cas had barely eaten in five days, had a fever of 105.7°F, and was in pain, which they somehow never noticed. They still sent him home on a Friday. We were told Internal Medicine only worked Tuesday through Friday, so instead of keeping a dangerously sick cat hospitalized, they sent him home for the weekend and told us to wait.

We did not wait. We took him to AMC, and the difference was night and day,  he had to be hospitalized, and he underwent a series of aggressive diagnostic testing to get to the bottom of his symptoms as soon as possible, this included an MRI and other invasive testing, and needed to have a feeding tube placed. He needed weeks of antibiotics. That was how sick he actually was. I am completely confident Cas would have died if we had followed BluePearl’s instructions. Thankfully AMC saved him and I am thankful to them and for our decision to go there.

Then, when we called at night to get his records from blue pearl, someone on the night shift hung up on us. A perfect ending to an already appalling experience.

Believe BluePearl’s reputation. We learned the hard way. Never again.
we love BluePearl, and professionalism and dedication they have!

Most amazing care for our fur baby. We are so grateful to Dr. Chen and staff. We had vet emergency that she took care of and was so informative and empathetic. We appreciate all her skill and compassion. Thank you! Sully 🐕 thanks even more. …
They’re very helpful and knowledgeable.

Incredibly mixed bag. They were great with our dog who had an immediate issue with poisoning, and they seemed to be better than VERG (an absolute nightmare). But our cat recently had what appeared to be VERY serious GI issues. Bloating, limited mobility, visibly and vocally distressed.

After a long and traumatizing first visit we were discharged with the reassurance that he would be okay, but little to nothing to say about his incredibly concerning symptoms. I tried calling in the following days bc he wasn't pooping at all in the 48+ hours after discharge and was still a little lethargic. I had a brief chat w someone at the front desk, but was told to go to a primary care vet if I wanted immediate answers. The problem is that our primary care vet was just going to send us back to the ER.

I got no follow-up calls to answer my serious questions about the cat's VERY serious symptoms. If someone would have just called back, we could have had a grounded convo about what our cat needed, but instead we were left to just come back and spend another 1200 dollars just to get answers (and meds) we could've gotten during the first visit, or even with a follow-up call.

I'm not mad about the care our cat got necessarily (just happy he'll be fine), just the way that our concerns were met with mixed answers and a general sense that they didn't want to have to deal with *another damn pet*. Also upset that we had to blow money on an unnecessary 2nd visit bc they always talk about being at capacity (is everyone running high volume businesses with skeleton crews these days? wtf). It's hard not to feel like we got worked a little, and that's very upsetting.
